headline: Tuesday close: software weakness meets a pivotal chip earnings test
quick: Twelve Data validated the completed November 17 1day bar for all twelve tracked stocks.
Nvidia results arrived after the cash close; the saved daily bar does not measure their reaction.

entries.happened: AAPL closed at $351.91, -0.25% against the prior close, on 37,341,600 shares versus a trailing average of 47,993,280. The daily range was $349.67 to $355.36. Apple’s newsroom listed November 17 entertainment updates, but no material financial event was verified for the cash session. Those content announcements do not establish an explanation for the measured stock move.
entries.why: Services growth and device replacement cycles must carry the valuation, while rising US real yields increase the return required from long-dated ecosystem cash flows. A quiet tape gives no new evidence on iPhone demand. Margin durability depends on product mix and services attach rates. A health research initiative might deepen engagement eventually, but it has no quantified revenue contribution and should not be used to explain Tuesday’s price. The measured -0.25% session return is one observation, and the volume comparison helps assess participation but cannot identify an investor motive. The next disclosure must test these operating mechanisms before the price is interpreted as a durable change in value.
entries.priced_in: At $351.91, the market price already reflects the completed November 17 trading session, but it does not reveal which of these operating expectations changed. The dated source is context, not an identified driver.

entries.next_date: Next scheduled earnings date not verified; watch the next company filing, product-demand data and completed cash session.

entries.happened: AMZN closed at $257.89, +0.05% against the prior close, on 38,499,300 shares versus a trailing average of 49,630,755. The daily range was $254.00 to $259.90. Amazon announced prepared meals through same-day grocery delivery on November 17, alongside a separate plan to invest $7 billion in renewable energy in India by 2030. entries.why: Prepared meals could add order frequency and basket size, but delivery economics, spoilage and fulfilment costs determine whether incremental sales translate into profit. The announcement gave availability, not a segment-level margin forecast. Energy investment can support AWS capacity and future operating costs, yet it also consumes capital before returns are visible. Investors need evidence that cloud demand and free cash flow absorb both data-centre and retail investment. The measured +0.05% session return is one observation, and the volume comparison helps assess participation but cannot identify an investor motive. The next disclosure must test these operating mechanisms before the price is interpreted as a durable change in value.

entries.happened: TSLA closed at $380.11, +0.10% against the prior close, on 22,138,200 shares versus a trailing average of 39,001,340. The daily range was $374.13 to $382.84. Tesla filed additional proxy materials on November 17, soliciting votes ahead of its December 3 annual meeting. The filing provides advocacy for board recommendations rather than independent proof of robot or vehicle economics. Separate the measurable vote outcome from claims about eventual commercial scale; near-flat trading is not a verdict on either. The measured +0.10% session return is one observation, and the volume comparison helps assess participation but cannot identify an investor motive. The next disclosure must test these operating mechanisms before the price is interpreted as a durable change in value.

entries.happened: MSFT closed at $506.24, -2.27% against the prior close, on 27,914,600 shares versus a trailing average of 26,850,970. The daily range was $496.51 to $515.64. Microsoft announced new Copilot, security-agent and Cobalt 200 cloud offerings at Ignite on November 17. Product breadth can improve retention without immediately improving unit economics. Cobalt 200 performance claims are product specifications, not evidence of customer margins. entries.happened: NVDA closed at $155.46, -0.44% against the prior close, on 398,625,600 shares versus a trailing average of 220,601,425. The daily range was $150.33 to $158.19. Nvidia closed its November 17 cash session before reporting fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion after the bell and guiding to $130.0 billion for the next quarter. entries.why: Data-centre revenue of $107.6 billion demonstrates exceptionally strong near-term demand, but investors must test how much of future accelerator spending becomes durable customer cash flow. Governance, export rules and customer financing remain separate risks; the next regular session is the first cash-market test. entries.happened: META closed at $618.87, -1.20% against the prior close, on 12,914,100 shares versus a trailing average of 23,526,980. The daily range was $613.51 to $627.48. Meta announced on November 17 that its Muse personal AI agent became available in Australia.
